screened.name: Lexus NX 350h
screened.reason: Standard FWD includes Lexus Safety System+ 3.0 and the standard power rear door; no Premium or hands-free-door option is selected. Rear space is adequate; long gear needs a verified carrier route.

screened.name: Mazda CX-50 Hybrid
screened.reason: Estimated absent for the selected Hybrid Preferred: the available equipment description supports MRCC, while CTS continuous centering is not established for this grade. Best estimate is adaptive cruise with corrective lane support, so centering input remains 0/5. This is estimated fitment, not a verified absence.

screened.name: Toyota RAV4 Hybrid
screened.reason: New generation, entry LE with Toyota Safety Sense 4.0. No power-door upgrade. Useful cabin and luggage area; FWD tires and clearance remain relevant for winter.

screened.name: Lexus UX 300h
screened.reason: Base seats are power adjustable; ventilation and the powered rear door belong to higher grades. Tight rear seating and luggage room constrain three-adult trips.

screened.name: BMW X3
screened.reason: The referenced $51,300 base + $3,450 Premium/assistance build exceeds $60k OTD after destination/tax/fees. A cheaper fully verified assisted build was not established; this is not a claim that every X3 is ineligible.

screened.name: Mazda CX-30
screened.reason: Turbo Premium Plus is the documented CTS grade; its turbo powertrain and 25-MPG EPA record replace the old non-turbo assumptions. Rear accommodation stays tight.

screened.name: Kia Sportage Hybrid
screened.reason: LX now includes stop/go cruise and LFA2. Cloth/manual-seat equipment is less plush than SX-Prestige, but avoids paying for the old power-door constraint.

screened.name: Mazda CX-5
screened.reason: The all-new 2026 Premium Plus explicitly includes CTS with Lane Change Assist and a power rear gate. Large touchscreen controls and actual ride/noise need a test drive.

screened.name: Hyundai IONIQ 5
screened.reason: Entry SE Standard Range has stop/go cruise and LFA. The 245-mile EPA range is not the long-range model. Spacious flat-floor cabin; manual rear gate at this trim.

screened.name: Ford Mustang Mach-E
screened.reason: Select retains adaptive cruise with lane centering. Technology Package and paid BlueCruise are unselected and receive no hands-free credit. Standard battery has 260 EPA miles.

screened.name: Honda CR-V Hybrid
screened.reason: Entry Sport hybrid includes Honda Sensing and Traffic Jam Assist without Sport-L liftgate pricing. Roomy cabin and straightforward controls; selected cloth/manual-gate equipment matters.

screened.name: Subaru Forester Hybrid
screened.reason: Revised entry hybrid price; EyeSight with lane centering, heated seats and standard powered rear gate. Useful roof/cargo packaging and 8.7-inch clearance; new hybrid longevity is uncertain, with confidence shown separately.

screened.name: Nissan Rogue Rock Creek
screened.reason: SV supplies ProPILOT and power liftgate without Rock Creek packaging. FWD is the cheaper reference build; its 32-MPG EPA record is not the Rock Creek AWD record.

screened.name: Nissan LEAF
screened.reason: Redesigned S+ includes hands-on ProPILOT and has 303 EPA miles. It is not the old CHAdeMO LEAF; Platinum wheels and power-door equipment are unselected.

screened.name: Hyundai Tucson Hybrid
screened.reason: Entry SE FWD has SCC and LFA with 38 MPG. Do not inherit Limited AWD features, powered gate or the AWD energy record.

screened.name: Subaru Solterra
screened.reason: 2026 range/charging and equipment update: 288-mile EPA reference, conventional powered gate, Driver Monitor and assisted lane changes are included. Limited kick activation is excluded.

screened.name: Toyota bZ
screened.reason: Entry XLE FWD uses the smaller battery and 236-mile EPA range; it is not FWD Plus or Limited AWD. Standard Toyota Safety Sense and powered rear door.

screened.name: Tesla Model Y
screened.reason: Cash price before savings/incentives. Paid FSD (Supervised) is selected and costed for five years; driver supervision is mandatory. Sparse physical controls constrain ergonomics.

screened.name: Kia EV6
screened.reason: Entry Light includes HDA and stop/go cruise. The standard-range 237-mile battery is selected; Wind AWD and its powered-hatch equipment are not borrowed.

screened.name: Acura RDX
screened.reason: Base RDX already has ACC, speed-limited LKAS and powered tailgate. No Technology-package price or acoustic-side-glass benefit is assumed. LKAS does not provide low-speed traffic-jam steering.

screened.name: BMW X2
screened.reason: Overlaps the X1 powertrain/price class with less carrying flexibility. X1 now includes a documented assistance package; no need to retain both.

screened.name: BMW X1
screened.reason: A manufacturer label establishes the $500 Driving Assistance Plus selection; retailer equipment description confirms ACC with steering assistance. No Professional/Technology package benefits are credited.

screened.name: Genesis GV70
screened.reason: Base 2.5T has heated power seats, powered liftgate, SCC and HDA. Leather, ventilation and higher-trim benefits are not assumed. Premium gasoline is costed.

screened.name: BMW 430i Gran Coupe
screened.reason: Original base build had no verified ACC/centering. Complete current assistance-package prerequisites and OTD not established; not labeled unavailable.

screened.name: Kia Niro Hybrid
screened.reason: EX is the first documented navigation-based SCC grade; LFA is standard. Its efficient wheel configuration uses the FE EPA record, not the old SX assumption.

screened.name: Mitsubishi Outlander
screened.reason: Old 2.5L/2024 assumptions do not establish the current 2026 equipment/powertrain. Current exact assisted configuration and price need re-verification.

screened.name: MINI Countryman S ALL4
screened.reason: MINI replaced by lower-cost practical hatchbacks and hybrids; no claim that the model is unavailable.

screened.name: Volvo XC40
screened.reason: Old Core build lacked verified Pilot Assist; a complete current package/trim quote was not established. No claim that every XC40 is ineligible.

screened.name: Mercedes-Benz GLA 250
screened.reason: Old base build lacked verified driving-assistance package. Current option prerequisites and total cost unresolved; do not rank an unverified build as an assisted option.

screened.name: Audi Q3
screened.reason: Old S line/current-page generation mismatch; named 2026 assisted package and current price not established. Manufacturer rolling page now shows 2027.

screened.name: Kia Seltos
screened.reason: SX is required for SCC/HDA. A powered liftgate requires an additional package that is not selected; useful AWD but ride/noise and compact back seat limit comfort.

screened.name: Jeep Compass
screened.reason: Old build relied on unselected assistance and ranked poorly on cost/comfort inputs. Broader manual-hatch and efficient sedan alternatives replace it; not declared unavailable.

screened.name: GMC Terrain
screened.reason: AT4 was selected around the old liftgate/utility constraints; replace this overlapping gas crossover with broader body styles and EV options. No Super Cruise capability inferred.

screened.name: Lincoln Corsair
screened.reason: Listed 2026 Premiere/Reserve cannot be purchased for California registration; OEM disclosure verified.

screened.name: Chevrolet Equinox
screened.reason: Gas RS + liftgate package no longer needed for eligibility. Equinox EV adds a materially different powertrain/value choice; not a claim that gas Equinox is unavailable.

screened.name: Volkswagen Tiguan
screened.reason: All-new Tiguan S has standard IQ.DRIVE/Travel Assist. The cheapest S FWD uses the distinct 29-MPG record; SE power-gate and 4MOTION features are unselected.

screened.name: Honda Civic Hybrid Hatchback
screened.reason: Added manual-hatch alternative. Sport Hybrid is the least expensive hybrid hatch, with ACC/LKAS/TJA. Low clearance and long-gear packaging constrain mountain use; no Touring equipment is borrowed.

screened.name: Toyota Prius
screened.reason: Entry LE is the 57-MPG configuration with TSS 3.0 and a manual hatch. Rear headroom, low seating and clearance should be checked with the third adult.

screened.name: Toyota Prius Plug-in Hybrid
screened.reason: SE has 44 EPA electric miles and TSS 3.0; the plug-in battery reduces luggage flexibility. The five-year scenario assumes regular nearby charging, not all-electric driving.

screened.name: Toyota Corolla Hybrid
screened.reason: Low-cost sedan with TSS 3.0 and 50 MPG. The conventional trunk and rear-adult space constrain three-person long-gear trips without excluding the car.

screened.name: Toyota Camry Hybrid
screened.reason: Roomier hybrid sedan with small wheels, TSS 3.0 and 51 MPG. Trunk access is less flexible than a hatch; rear seats and ski pass-through need an actual fit check.

screened.name: Honda Accord Hybrid
screened.reason: Entry hybrid Sport includes Honda Sensing/TJA. Large rear seating area and trunk are useful, but low clearance and 19-inch wheels constrain ride/winter use.

screened.name: Hyundai Elantra Hybrid
screened.reason: Current feature matrix restricts SCC to Limited despite LFA on every trim. Select Limited with its upgraded seats; do not mistake LFA-only availability for an adaptive-cruise package. Compact trunk access and low clearance limit long-gear use.

screened.name: Hyundai Sonata Hybrid
screened.reason: Blue supplies SCC/LFA without Limited pricing and returns 51 MPG. Smart trunk release is not a powered liftgate; rear-adult room is useful but roof/gear fit remains conditional.

screened.name: Mazda3 Hatchback
screened.reason: This is the documented CTS automatic hatch configuration. Turbo AWD has a 26-MPG EPA record; no power hatch. Rear space and low clearance constrain three-adult mountain trips.

screened.name: Volkswagen Golf GTI
screened.reason: S includes IQ.DRIVE/Travel Assist and automatic DSG. Supportive sport seats suit some drivers, but a firmer ride and low clearance are relevant comfort/winter tradeoffs.

screened.name: Subaru Impreza
screened.reason: Entry Sport has EyeSight with lane centering and AWD. Manual hatch is allowed; clearance is lower than Crosstrek despite the traction system.

screened.name: Subaru Crosstrek Hybrid
screened.reason: New conventional hybrid, not the older plug-in Crosstrek. EyeSight, AWD and 8.7-inch clearance help winter access; actual rear/luggage fit is still conditional.

screened.name: Toyota Corolla Cross Hybrid
screened.reason: Entry hybrid S includes TSS 3.0 and AWD. Modest rear space and manual-gate equipment keep the price below an unnecessary liftgate upgrade.

screened.name: Honda HR-V
screened.reason: LX has Honda Sensing with ACC/LKAS, so EX-L is unnecessary for assistance. Modest 2.0L power and rear-seat/cargo fit need a loaded-trip check.

screened.name: Chevrolet Equinox EV
screened.reason: Estimated absent for the selected base LT1: the available trim evidence supports ACC and corrective lane keeping. The manual describes optional Hands-On Steering Assist with connected-plan conditions; base-grade fitment/entitlement is not established. Best estimate is no continuous centering (0/5), rather than crediting an unselected option. This is estimated fitment, not a verified absence.

screened.name: Chevrolet Bolt
screened.reason: New 2027 Bolt is on sale with 262 EPA miles and standard ACC. Super Cruise needs extra packages; no centering credit or paid entitlement is inferred for base LT.

screened.name: Tesla Model 3
screened.reason: Cash price before savings/incentives. Five years of $99/month FSD (Supervised) are explicitly costed; driver supervision is mandatory. Conventional trunk and sparse controls affect utility/ergonomics.

screened.name: Hyundai Tucson Plug-in Hybrid
screened.reason: SEL provides SCC/LFA, powered gate and 32 EPA electric miles. PHEV carries extra systems and the electric-mile split is a scenario assumption.

screened.name: Kia Sportage Plug-in Hybrid
screened.reason: Entry X-Line PHEV has SCC/LFA and powered gate, with 33 EPA electric miles. Not the more expensive X-Line Prestige equipment list.

screened.name: Toyota RAV4 Plug-in Hybrid
screened.reason: Redesigned SE plug-in offers 54 EPA electric miles, a standard power liftgate and TSS 4.0. Do not reuse the old RAV4 Prime environmental score or higher-grade charging/comfort equipment.

screened.name: Kia K4 Hatchback
screened.reason: Affordable manual-hatch alternative with standard stop/go SCC and LFA. EX 2.0L uses the 30-MPG EPA record, not the turbo model.

screened.name: Hyundai IONIQ 6
screened.decision: Held out: current new inventory needed
screened.reason: No regular 2026 US model in the checked EPA data; manufacturer-confirmed discontinuation reported by Edmunds. Remaining new 2025 stock requires an actual current quote; N is not a substitute configuration.

screened.name: Toyota Sienna
screened.reason: Eight-seat hybrid minivan, power sliding doors and liftgate. Fold the third row and retain a second-row adult; long gear still needs an actual fit check.

screened.name: Honda Odyssey
screened.reason: Leather/heated front seats, sliding second row and folding third row provide a distinct people-and-gear option. LKAS is speed-limited and does not supply low-speed traffic-jam steering.

screened.name: Kia Carnival Hybrid
screened.reason: Hybrid minivan with power sliding doors and a manual rear liftgate at LXS. Three-row packaging adds useful interior carrying space without crediting EX/SX liftgate equipment.

screened.name: Ford Maverick Hybrid
screened.reason: Compact hybrid pickup with heated front seats and a short open bed. AWD Lariat uses its own 36-MPG EPA record, not the 38-MPG FWD record. Weatherproof gear storage is extra.

screened.name: Hyundai Santa Cruz
screened.reason: Turbo AWD compact pickup with XRT clearance/traction features, heated fronts and open-bed carrying flexibility. Rear accommodation is tighter than a minivan; test the third adult and gear.

screened.name: Subaru Outback
screened.reason: Redesigned 2.5L AWD SUV with 8.7-inch clearance, a long cargo area and power rear gate. It remains a useful wagon-like alternative but Subaru classifies it as an SUV.

screened.name: Toyota Crown Signia
screened.reason: Two-row hybrid SUV with a long load area and heated/ventilated leather front seats. Wagon-like utility does not make it a manufacturer-classified wagon. No Advanced Technology package is selected.

screened.name: Hyundai Santa Fe Hybrid
screened.reason: Entry three-row hybrid with cloth seats and a powered liftgate. SE receives ordinary SCC/LFA, not higher-grade navigation-based cruise or HDA2 lane changes.

screened.name: Kia Sorento Hybrid
screened.reason: Three-row hybrid with heated fronts and a power tailgate. Keep the third row folded for three adults plus mountain gear; its smaller cabin does not receive minivan carrying credit.

screened.name: Toyota Highlander Hybrid
screened.reason: Three-row AWD hybrid with heated front seats and powered liftgate. Third-row passenger use competes with luggage; the assessed mountain scenario retains one second-row adult.

screened.name: Honda Pilot
screened.reason: Three-row V6 SUV in entry Sport FWD trim. Cloth seats, power tailgate and Traffic Jam Assist are assessed; TrailSport AWD, tires and acoustic upgrades are unselected.

screened.name: Hyundai Palisade
screened.reason: Redesigned three-row V6 SUV with cloth seats and powered liftgate. SE includes navigation-based cruise and forward-attention warning; no HDA2 assisted lane change or Calligraphy comfort equipment is credited.

screened.name: Ford Ranger
screened.reason: Held out: the checked 2026 US order guide establishes ACC and lane keeping, but not continuous lane centering in the proposed XLT package. Do not confuse corrective support with centering; no complete eligible assisted build established.

screened.name: Chrysler Pacifica Plug-in Hybrid
screened.reason: Held out: discontinued-model notice and remaining-stock uncertainty. A 2026 EPA record alone does not establish an orderable new assisted configuration; a current local build/quote would be needed.

screened.name: Volvo V60 wagon
screened.reason: Wagon coverage gap: no current assisted new US V60 build at or below $60k OTD was established. Outback and Crown Signia are manufacturer-classified SUVs, so neither is relabeled to fill the gap. Older-model new inventory needs an actual quote.

screened.name: Toyota GR86 Manual
screened.reason: Base 6MT RWD. Tiny rear seats and a folding rear seatback prevent a credible three-adults-plus-long-gear plan; retain a minimum carrying estimate.

screened.name: Mazda MX-5 Miata Manual
screened.reason: Sport soft top 6MT RWD. Only two seats: cannot transport the three adults in the mountain scenario, regardless of external gear storage.

screened.name: Honda Civic Si Manual
screened.reason: Si 6MT FWD. Three adults are possible, but low clearance and sedan long-gear access constrain winter usefulness; measure actual gear fit.

screened.name: Volkswagen ID.4 AWD
screened.reason: AWD Pro, 19-inch wheels. Useful rear-seat/cargo packaging; AWD and moderate clearance help access, but no route-specific winter charging study establishes a trip upgrade.

screened.name: Hyundai IONIQ 5 SEL AWD
screened.reason: SEL AWD, 19-inch wheels. Useful crossover space and AWD; 290-mile EPA range is not loaded winter range. SEL ground clearance is not XRT clearance.

screened.name: Toyota Tacoma
screened.reason: SR5 Double Cab 4WD 8AT, 5-ft bed. Double Cab retains a rear adult; bed needs secure weatherproof gear storage. Four-wheel drive and clearance aid access without establishing winter braking grip.

screened.name: Nissan Ariya AWD
screened.decision: Held out: current new-stock eligibility unresolved
screened.reason: 2025 Engage e-4ORCE considered. Nissan discontinued US Ariya after 2025; California VIN lead JN8CF0BF6SM761659 redirects to general inventory. Other leads are demo-site duplicates or used stock. A current new California listing/quote is needed before ranking; no 2026 US build is invented.

commute.note: Assessment of the selected Lexus Safety System+ 3.0: DRCC and Lane Tracing Assist. Component estimates describe supported commuting tasks and supervision, not measured safety or exact-build road-test performance.

component_notes: 4/5: selected adaptive cruise supports stop/go following. Automatic restart has operating limits; longer stops can require driver confirmation. No extra navigation or intersection-handling benefit is assumed.

4/5: selected continuous lane centering covers ordinary highway following, with low-speed assistance where supported. It is supervised steering assistance; complex intersections and automatic lane changes are not credited.

3/5: baseline supervised, hands-on operation and driver-facing status/alerts. A generic attention or drowsiness warning is not treated as camera-based gaze monitoring. No independent exact-build usability result is claimed.
commute.review_note: Reviewed 2026-11-16: documented tasks and supervision features are scored. Test reports are context; feature count is not measured steering quality, intervention frequency, safety or driver satisfaction.

mountain.note: Standard FWD includes Lexus Safety System+ 3.0 and the standard power rear door; no Premium or hands-free-door option is selected. Rear space is adequate; long gear needs a verified carrier route.
mountain.interior_fit: Unmeasured: retain one rear adult plus boots/bags and check a partial seat-fold/pass-through against actual ski/board dimensions. Published cargo volume alone does not establish fit.
mountain.roof: Candidate carrier route is unverified: confirm exact roof option, feet/bars, dynamic load, carrier capacity and hatch/trunk clearance before purchase. No roof equipment is assumed included.
mountain.winter: Selected two-wheel-drive build needs appropriate winter tires/chains and a clearance check; traction equipment is not inferred from the body style.
mountain.trip: Fuel stops are straightforward; loaded climbing, cold and roof drag raise consumption. No exact winter-trip range is claimed.
component_notes: 3/5: Moderate carrying estimate; retain the rear adult and check long-gear access and bags together. Selected configuration: Standard FWD. This is an editorial packaging estimate, not a measured fit.

2/5: Selected two-wheel-drive crossover, or low-clearance AWD car, has access limitations; body style or AWD alone does not remove them. EPA drivetrain: Front-Wheel Drive. Winter tires and compliant traction devices are not assumed included.

5/5: rapid liquid-fuel replenishment baseline, not an overall mountain-trip rating. Fuel availability and consumption on the actual route still need checking; carrying and winter access are scored separately.
mountain.review_note: Trip inputs reviewed 2026-11-15 across the full cohort. Carrying, winter access and replenishment are distinct judgments. Exact gear fit and route-specific performance remain unverified; no extra brand, AWD or redesign bonus is applied.
